dermatology.title: RD005 Emollient preferred product list
dermatology.fact: A preferred list of products to be used first line: Cetraben lotion; Epimax Original, Epimax ExCetra, Aquamax, QV and Cetraben creams; Epimax, Hydromol and Cetraben ointments; Dermol cream and Dermol 500 lotion; ImuDERM. Epimax Oatmeal is marked second line, if other emollients are not tolerated. Where a specialist advises a bath or shower product, the first-line products are Hydromol Bath & Shower, QV Gentle Wash or Aquamax Wash. QV Cream is listed at £5.96 per 500g (Drug Tariff March 2021 prices).
dermatology.quote: the recommended first-line products would be Hydromol® Bath & Shower, QV® Gentle Wash or Aquamax® Wash
dermatology.use: QV Cream and QV Gentle Wash are both on the first-line list here. The document prints named company contacts: use the link, never copy those details.

dermatology.org: Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West ICB
dermatology.title: BOB ICB Emollient Guideline, version 1.0
dermatology.fact: No first-line or second-line tiers; products are grouped by light, medium and heavy emollient, with an asterisk on the most cost-effective options (Epimax Original, Isomol, ExCetra and ointment, 50:50 and emulsifying ointment, Hydromol Intensive, Dermol 500). QV Skin Lotion is listed under light emollients, without the asterisk. Zerodouble gel is marked 2nd line and Cetraben ointment not 1st line. Cetraben cream, Diprobase Advanced Eczema cream and Epaderm ointment are Green Restricted due to cost; Oilatum cream and Doublebase gel have Block status. The guideline replaced the three previous place-based guidelines.
dermatology.quote: QV Skin Lotion (white soft paraffin 5%) 500ml pump
dermatology.use: QV is on the list but not marked cost-effective. Review due January 2027: the window to make a case is before then.

dermatology.title: Sheffield skin formulary choices: Abbreviated guide to emollients used in primary care
dermatology.date: Approved by Formulary Subgroup and Area Prescribing Group January 2023
dermatology.fact: Ranked by product type. Creams: 1st Epimax Original, 2nd Epimax ExCetra, 3rd ZeroAQS. Ointments: 1st Fifty:50, 2nd AproDerm, 3rd Zeroderm. Gels: 1st Epimax Isomol, 2nd AproDerm gel, 3rd MyriBase. Lotions: 1st QV skin lotion, 2nd Cetraben lotion. Colloidal oat: 1st Epimax oatmeal cream, 2nd Miclaro, 3rd AproDerm. QV Intensive Ointment is listed among the ointment alternatives. The printed review date, January 2026, has passed.
dermatology.use: QV skin lotion is the first-line lotion here. The review date has passed, so the next version could move it either way.

dermatology.quote: Green – First line. Any AHP to prescribe.

dermatology.title: North East London Emollient Prescribing Guidelines for Primary Care, version 1.1
dermatology.date: Ratified 17/12/2024 by the NEL Integrated Medicines Optimisation and Prescribing Committee
dermatology.fact: First line (cost-effective choices, under £5/500g): Epimax ointment, EmulsifEss, white soft paraffin, 50:50, Epimax Original, AproDerm cream, ointment and gel, Hydrous ointment (Aquaderm), Zeroderm, Epimax Isomol, Epimax Moisturising, ZeroAQS and Zerocream. emergency-and-urgent-care.title: Relationship between time spent in emergency departments, employment, and hospitalisation, England: 2021 to 2025
emergency-and-urgent-care.fact: Among working-age employees who attended a type 1 emergency department (ED) in England between April 2021 and March 2023, 37.0% were hospitalised more than one day after leaving the ED and 21.9% left employment within two years. After adjusting for clinical and demographic factors, later hospital admission was 6.0% higher for two to under four hours in the ED and 95.0% higher for 12 hours or more, compared with under two hours. ONS states these are associations, not causal relationships.
emergency-and-urgent-care.quote: this was 95.0% higher for individuals who spent 12 hours or more in the ED, compared with those who spent under two hours in the ED
emergency-and-urgent-care.use: Official evidence that long ED stays go with later admissions, for a flow, triage or discharge conversation. Associations only: do not say long waits cause admissions.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Musculoskeletal elective treatment waiting times and labour market outcomes, England: 2014 to 2025
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Among working-age NHS patients having elective inpatient treatment for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in England between April 2015 and March 2023, each extra four weeks of waiting reduced annual earnings by up to £487 (other joint disorders), £392 (other MSK conditions), £329 (back, neck and MSK pain) and £301 (osteoarthritis). ONS found no statistical evidence of a link between waiting time and later employment status or benefit receipt.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: each additional four weeks of waiting led to a £487 reduction in annual earnings in the fourth year after treatment
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A cost-of-waiting figure for elective orthopaedic recovery and theatre throughput conversations.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board (via NWSSP)

orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: four-year sole supply commitment for knee implants with Zimmer Biomet

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: HTG743: Robot-assisted surgery for orthopaedic procedures, early value assessment
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted knee or hip replacement: ApolloKnee, CORI, Mako SmartRobotics, ROSA Knee, SkyWalker and VELYS. Use is conditional on evidence being generated under NICE's evidence generation plan and on regulatory approval including NHS England's Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC) approval. The evidence generation period is 3 years, after which NICE will assess whether routine adoption is appropriate. NICE has renumbered the content from Health technology evaluation 22 to HealthTech guidance 743, unchanged.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted surgery for knee or hip replacements.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Robot-assisted knee and hip surgery is allowed only while evidence is generated. A rep selling a robot needs to know the evidence plan commitments.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) and British Orthopaedic Association (BOA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Five high-volume, low-complexity (HVLC) orthopaedic pathways updated
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GIRFT updated five national elective pathways with the BOA and specialist societies: total primary hip replacement; total and unicompartmental primary knee replacement; Dupuytren's disease; shoulder arthroscopy for rotator cuff repair or subacromial decompression; hallux valgus and rigidus. First issued in 2020. The 2026 updates align the follow-up sections with GIRFT's Further Faster Follow-Up Protocols and Standardising Follow-Up guidance. A joint GIRFT and BOA webinar is on 13 October 2026, 1pm to 2pm.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: it is imperative that all teams across England adopt them
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The pathways set how clinics and theatres are run for the five highest-volume elective procedures, which shapes what trusts buy and when.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: MHRA orthopaedic Device Safety Information (DSI) since 2024
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GOV.UK's Device Safety Information list tagged Orthopaedics returns these implant items: DSI/2026/010 Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements (26 August 2026); DSI/2026/001 M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc, Spinal Kinetics, new monitoring for osteolysis (15 January 2026); DSI/2025/005 Profemur cobalt chrome modular neck hip replacements (4 September 2025); DSI/2024/007 CPT Hip System femoral stem 12/14 neck taper, periprosthetic femoral fracture (4 September 2024); DSI/2024/005 Symbios ORIGIN posterior stabilised patient-matched total knee, early revision (23 April 2024); DSI/2024/002 MAGEC X System, UK suspension lifted (12 March 2024). The same list holds one non-implant item, DSI/2026/003 on blood transfusion giving sets.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements: risk of metal-wear effects and revision surgery (DSI/2026/010)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A standing list of recent implant safety actions a rep can be asked about at any trust.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: DSI/2026/010: cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements, all withdrawn before 2019
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: An MHRA investigation of every hip replacement with a cobalt-chrome modular neck ever sold in the UK found increased wear and corrosion risk and a possible increase in revision for adverse local tissue reaction. All of these devices were removed from the market before 2019 and none remain commercially available. MHRA advises trusts to use the National Joint Registry (NJR) and local records to identify patients and invite them for virtual or face-to-face review; symptomatic patients annually, asymptomatic patients on a patient-initiated follow-up pathway. Table 1 (NJR data extracted June 2026) covers Aesculap Metha modular, LimaCorporate H-Max-M, Smith and Nephew SMF, Stryker ABG II modular and Symbios HARMONY modular and SPS modular. The advice for distributors is that there is none.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: there is no advice for distributors regarding this DSI
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: This is a patient-recall workload for trusts, not a product-switching event: the devices are off the market and distributors have no action. Do not frame it as a competitor opening.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: NJR 23rd Annual Report 2026: hips, knees and robotic use (surgical data to 31 December 2025)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Primary hip replacements using unipolar implants reached 113,472 in 2025, a record for the fourth year running. Primary knee replacements reached a record 143,972 in 2025; NHS-funded procedures in NHS facilities have plateaued and now represent less than 50% of knee volume, against over 60% historically. Robotic procedures recorded in 2025: 3,762 hip and 11,641 knee. Mako was the most-used knee system (7,869) followed by CORI (1,590); CORI use roughly doubled since 2023; VELYS had its first recorded use in 2024; six knee systems have data recorded. Robotic hip replacement rose from 2,854 in 2023 to 3,762 in 2025.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: ANNUAL REPORT 2026
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Current national volumes and the robotics share for sizing a hip or knee patch. The NJR does not publish a market-size value.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Referral to Treatment (RTT) waiting times: Trauma and Orthopaedic Service (C_110) by trust
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: NHS England publishes monthly RTT provider files by treatment function; the latest on the 2026-27 page is July 2026. In the July 2026 full extract, Trauma and Orthopaedic Service is treatment function code C_110, with rows for completed admitted and non-admitted pathways, incomplete pathways, incomplete pathways with a decision to admit, and new RTT periods, at provider and commissioner level. This entry gives the source only; it states no waiting-list total.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Incomplete pathways are waiting times for cases where patients are still waiting to start treatment at the end of the month.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The standing source for trust-level orthopaedic waiting pressure. Pull the C_110 rows for a named trust before quoting any figure.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: GIRFT Orthopaedic Surgery workstream: reports, pathways and news
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: GIRFT's Orthopaedic Surgery page describes two published reports (2015 and a February 2020 follow-up) and names Professor Tim Briggs as clinical lead. The 2020 follow-up headline findings include a reduction in revision rates every year since 2012 and a 20% reduction in average length of stay, releasing more than 368,000 bed days. The site is behind a bot check, so scripts cannot read it, but a normal browser can.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: A reduction in revision rates every year since 2012
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The entry point for GIRFT's orthopaedic pathways and news. Trust-level GIRFT data is not public.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: TOS3 Customer Engagement Guide: what Lots 2 and 3 cover
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Lot 2 Equipment includes, but is not limited to: robotics, navigation, imaging, fluid management, consoles and arthroscopic stack systems, power tools, helmets (hoods/togas), tourniquet machines, bone harvesting/milling, ultrasound cement removal, cement mixing and ultrasound bone healing; consumables for equipment are in sub-lot 1.11. Lot 3 Services and Solutions includes, but is not limited to: wearable devices, patient/surgeon applications, software solutions, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technology, efficiency programmes, patient planning, managed equipment services and technical support.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: The consumables for equipment are found within sub lot 1.11.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The authoritative list of what counts as equipment and services on TOS3. It is wider than the shorthand 'robotics, navigation, power tools'.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: TOS4 pipeline notice 2026/S 000-016123: the earlier notice, with a superseded tender date

orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Publication date of tender notice (estimated)

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: SBS10238 Surgical Robots, Consumables and Related Services: a separate robotics route that names orthopaedics
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: Framework SBS10238 is active 24 May 2023 to 23 May 2027 and open to all NHS organisations in the UK. Its page lists orthopaedics among the specialties surgical robots serve (with urology, colorectal and gynaecology). It allows a further competition or direct award under Regulation 33 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. Three suppliers are named: CMR Surgical Limited, Intuitive Surgical Ltd and Medtronic. The page does not say which of them supply orthopaedic systems, so whether the framework is a route for hip or knee robots is not verified. TOS3 Lot 2 also lists robotics.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Via this framework agreement, you can run a further competition, or choose to direct award to a supplier
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A second robotics route exists outside TOS3. Check with SBS which of its three suppliers cover orthopaedic systems before telling a trust it is an option.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Contracts Finder: where trust TOS3 call-offs are published
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The Kettering, Northampton and Oxford TOS3 call-offs cited in this list were published on Contracts Finder as 'Call-off from a framework agreement' notices, each carrying contract start and end dates and a value. The search page accepts keywords across contract title, description and buyer. Search for 'TOS3' and for 'Lot 1.' (sub-lot numbers) to find further call-offs.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Can include contract title, description and buyer
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The place to find which trust has called off which TOS3 sub-lot, and when the call-off ends.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: MHRA weekly Field Safety Notices page
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: MHRA publishes manufacturers' Field Safety Notices (FSNs) as one page a week. The latest at this check is 'Field Safety Notices: 21 to 25 September 2026', published 29 September 2026. Entries give manufacturer, product, date and MHRA reference and are not tagged by device type; the page includes, for example, F.H. Industrie CALCANAIL threaded cannulated screw (5 September 2026). MHRA says it publishes them for information only and a recipient must act on a notice from the manufacturer.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: If you receive a field safety notice (FSN) from a manufacturer you must always act on it.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Where a recall or correction on an orthopaedic product first appears publicly. Scan by manufacturer name each week.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: ODEP product ratings: hip, knee and other implants
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: ODEP's products page lists rated implant components with component name, material and a 'Next ODEP Review Due' field, searchable by supplier and filterable by rating. The site also has pages for Beyond Compliance implants, digital certificates and procurement. Ratings are not restated here; read the entry for the product concerned.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: Next ODEP Review Due
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: A surgeon or procurement lead will ask for an implant's ODEP rating. Check the product's entry and its review due date before a conversation.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: NHFD 2026 annual report, 'Mind the Gap', and live key performance indicators
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The 2026 NHFD annual report, on 2025 data, was published 10 September 2026 and highlights continued variation in hip fracture care across hospitals. The key performance indicator page, annualised on 70,699 cases to the end of August 2026, shows: admission to specialist ward 10%; prompt orthogeriatric review 90%; prompt surgery 57%; NICE-compliant surgery 71%; promptly out of bed 82%; not delirious post-operatively 68%; return to original residence 75%; bone medication 62%.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: NHFD Report 2026 (10 September 2026)
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: National benchmarks for hip fracture care, relevant to trauma implants and orthogeriatric pathway conversations.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: Hospital Admitted Patient Care Activity 2025-26: procedure and provider tables
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: The 2025-26 publication covers 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 and records 22.6 million finished consultant episodes, up 71,455 (0.3%) on 2024-25. Downloads on the page include a procedures-and-interventions table, a provider table (hospital trusts) and a specialty table. Procedure counts are by operation code, so each code must be matched to a named procedure before a figure is quoted; this entry states no orthopaedic count.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: In 2025-26 there were 22.6 million FCEs recorded.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: The source for national and trust procedure volumes by operation code once the codes are mapped.

orthopaedics-and-trauma.title: GIRFT surgical hub accreditation: 83 hubs by June 2026, 125 in operation
orthopaedics-and-trauma.fact: At cohort 12 (announced 1 June 2026) the total accredited since March 2023 was 83. GIRFT runs quarterly cohorts aiming to accredit all 125 hubs in operation in England. The scheme is run with the Royal College of Surgeons and supported by the Royal College of Anaesthetists. Hubs focus on high-volume, low-complexity surgery including trauma and orthopaedics (including spinal surgery). Cohort 12's hubs include the Essex and Suffolk Elective Orthopaedic Centre, Pontefract Hospital Elective Orthopaedic Centre and Hampshire Elective Orthopaedic Centre. Earlier cohort announcements are on the same site.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.quote: GIRFT is running quarterly cohorts to accredit all 125 hubs currently in operation across the NHS in England.
orthopaedics-and-trauma.use: Surgical hubs are where much elective orthopaedic volume is moving. This names accredited orthopaedic centres and the programme's target.

pain-management.title: Musculoskeletal elective treatment waiting times and labour market outcomes, England: 2014 to 2025
pain-management.fact: Among working-age NHS patients having elective inpatient treatment for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in England between April 2015 and March 2023, each extra four weeks of waiting reduced annual earnings by up to £487 (other joint disorders), £392 (other MSK conditions), £329 (back, neck and MSK pain) and £301 (osteoarthritis). ONS found no statistical evidence of a link between waiting time and later employment status or benefit receipt.
pain-management.quote: For patients with "back, neck and MSK pain", the largest reduction in annual earnings for each additional four weeks of waiting time was of £329, in the third year after treatment
pain-management.use: A cost-of-waiting figure for back, neck and MSK pain pathway conversations.

frailty-and-older-people.title: Deaths registered in England and Wales: 2025
frailty-and-older-people.fact: 570,988 deaths were registered in England and Wales in 2025, 0.4% more than in 2024. Dementia and Alzheimer's disease was the leading cause, with 72,272 deaths (12.7% of all deaths): 16.5% of female deaths and 9.1% of male deaths. The age-standardised mortality rate was 913 per 100,000, the lowest since the series began in 1994. The North East had the highest age-standardised rates in England for both males (1,189) and females (880).
frailty-and-older-people.quote: Dementia and Alzheimer's disease continued to be the leading cause of death in England and Wales, with 72,272 deaths registered (12.7% of all deaths)
frailty-and-older-people.use: Scale of dementia as the leading cause of death, and where mortality is highest, for older-people and care-setting conversations.

cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.title: Deaths registered in England and Wales: 2025
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.fact: Ischaemic heart diseases were the leading cause of death among males in England and Wales in 2025, accounting for 12.2% of male deaths registered. Across all deaths, the leading cause was dementia and Alzheimer's disease (12.7%).
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.quote: Among males, ischaemic heart diseases were the leading cause of death, accounting for 12.2% of deaths registered in 2025.
cardiology-and-cardiac-surgery.use: Headline burden figure for coronary heart disease in men.
